x_posts.content:
Wool doesn't need a wash after one wear. Hang it, air it overnight, brush off the dust, and wash only when it actually stains. Most jackets die in the washing machine, not on your back.

https://man.empyre.site

Most men don't need more clothes. They need fewer in better cloth: two trousers, a jacket that fits through the shoulder, and shirts worth mending. A small rotation means every piece gets worn, which is what makes it worth buying in the first place.

The shoulder seam decides most of a shirt's fit. It should sit at the edge of your shoulder, not slide halfway down your arm. Get the shoulders right and the shirt reads tailored even off the rack. Get them wrong and no other alteration fixes it.

Most outfits don't need more pieces. They need the belt to match the shoe leather and the trouser hem to sit clean over the shoe. Fix those two details and the same clothes read as chosen, not thrown on.
Man of All the clothing for those who are the Jack's of ALL TRADES coming soon...
